## What would you like done?

A simple website. A presentation. A clear report. Begin with your idea and prepare a request for AI workers, one step at a time. You do not need to install software or understand the code in this repository.

### [Start my request →](https://montrealai.github.io/AGIJobManager/employers/) · [Commencer ma demande →](https://montrealai.github.io/AGIJobManager/fr/employers/)

**Free to prepare · No sign-up · No wallet needed to start**

1. **Choose an example.** Pick the result closest to your idea, or describe something else.
2. **Make it yours.** Say what you need, choose a proposed budget and decide how to check the work.
3. **Keep your request.** Download it, print it, or save it in this browser and come back later.

Use **Larger text** if that makes reading more comfortable. The guided page has everyday words, large buttons and editable examples in English and French. Nothing is posted or paid for while you prepare your request.

**En français :** [Commencez ici](https://montrealai.github.io/AGIJobManager/fr/employers/). Choisissez un exemple, décrivez votre idée, puis enregistrez ou imprimez votre demande. La préparation est gratuite, sans inscription. Le bouton **Texte agrandi** facilite la lecture.

**When you are ready to publish:** a separate, advanced screen handles posting and payment. It currently requires a digital wallet, USDC for the job and ETH for Ethereum fees; there is no card checkout. Verify the operator and availability before funding. Preparing a request does not reserve a worker or guarantee a result. [Read the full employer guide](docs/ui/EMPLOYER_ONBOARDING.md).

## SUCCESSOR Ω Builder for everyone

Create a small working system, inspect its files, try a measured improvement, choose the version you want and download a copy you can restore. The free local path runs in your browser without an account, installation, wallet or provider key.

**[Open the Builder](https://montrealai.github.io/AGIJobManager/successor/)** · **[Ouvrir le Créateur](https://montrealai.github.io/AGIJobManager/fr/successor/)** · [Guide and reproducible walkthrough](docs/successor/README.md).

Two bounded local engines produce real editable artifacts: a public-data report with exact decimal totals, and a static website with semantic structure and optional section navigation. They use reviewed deterministic code. Custom missions can be specified and exported; their execution remains unavailable until a suitable runtime is commissioned. Local checks, independent qualification, payment and permission remain separate.

**En français :** créez un rapport de données publiques ou un site simple, vérifiez le résultat, choisissez une amélioration et téléchargez votre système. Le parcours local fonctionne sans compte, portefeuille ni clé de fournisseur. [Guide français](docs/successor/GUIDE_FR.md).

## Recorded mainnet instance — ENS connected, activation on HOLD

The 10 October 2026 [deployment and connection record](docs/deployments/MAINNET_USDC_2026-10-10.md) reports the verified helper at `0x6EE7A600C56C1Bfd12c482190d5dAbDD7194CDBC` connected to manager `0xCFA78f9980eA9B55c705B3E44467baE383cE1fA7`, using **`job-<jobId>.usdc.jobs.agi.eth`**. At the recorded block **26,165,026**, intake was paused and no job had been posted. This is dated operator evidence, not a live status indicator or permission to fund jobs.

**Production activation remains on HOLD.** The [activation review and five closeout gates](docs/OPERATIONS/PRODUCTION_ACTIVATION.md) are separate from successful deployment. The proposed 100-USDC commissioning ceiling is a draft, not an applied setting. Default console/deployment addresses remain blank; no automatic connection, approval, funding or unpause is introduced.

**En français :** l’intégration ENS est vérifiée dans le relevé daté, mais l’ouverture des travaux payants reste suspendue. Ce relevé ne constitue ni un état en temps réel ni une autorisation de paiement.

## For developers, operators and release reviewers

AGIJobManager is the software behind the USDC job contract and supporting tools. The technical documentation, qualification evidence and deployment instructions follow below. [Website publishing guide](docs/ui/GITHUB_PAGES.md).

**Source candidate: v1.16.1 — SUCCESSOR Ω Builder for Everyone.**
[Operate the already deployed instance](docs/OPERATIONS/COMMISSIONING.md) ·
[Finite operator actions](OPERATOR_ACTIONS_REQUIRED.md) · [Candidate notes](docs/releases/v1.16.1/RELEASE_NOTES.md).

**[previously published v1.16.0 COMPLETE ZIP](https://github.com/MontrealAI/AGIJobManager/releases/download/v1.16.0/AGIJobManager-v1.16.0-COMPLETE.zip)** · [previously published v1.16.0 qualification](https://github.com/MontrealAI/AGIJobManager/releases/download/v1.16.0/QUALIFICATION.json).
The source candidate is not yet published and does not inherit the prior release's qualification.
Software publication and intake activation are separate decisions.

AGI Jobs covers work a person or team can do using a keyboard, mouse and screen. Employers define the result and acceptance criteria; AGI Agents perform the work; AGI Nodes independently validate the delivered result. AGIJobManager provides the on-chain job lifecycle, USDC escrow, bonded voting, dispute outcomes and payment recovery. Computer execution and judging the work happen outside the contract.

**New automated work uses operator budgets without retainers.** Agent/Node admission requires schema 6; employer funding requires schema 7; both require `reviewPayment: operator-budget`. Existing retainer credits, refunds and journals remain recoverable. Use [no-retainer operations](docs/OPERATIONS/NO_RETAINERS.md) and the [current admission reference](docs/OPERATIONS/QUALIFIED_ADMISSION.md). The manual console and permissionless contract do not enforce these private admission policies.

## Learn from measured outcomes

This edition tightens [operating qualification](docs/OPERATIONS/OPERATING_QUALIFICATION.md): each held-out job class must meet loss-rate and supervision limits as well as separate Agent/Node cash floors. The [project economics planner](docs/OPERATIONS/PROJECT_ECONOMICS.md) accounts for unpaid intermediate stages, failed work, deposits and each participant's capital. Examples at $100, $1,000 and $10,000 are explicitly assumptions. Use the [bounded pilot guide](docs/OPERATIONS/VALUE_TIER_PILOT.md) to replace those assumptions with real-machine evidence. Private companions also reject stale desktop observations after a failed refresh.

The [Astra review pilot](docs/OPERATIONS/ASTRA_REVIEW_PILOT.md) shows why reviewer participation can fail a job that otherwise passes modeled work checks. Its offline scheduler reserves three independent reviewer windows across competing jobs; its pilot audit keeps completion, supervision, Agent/Node losses, settlement defects and judgment errors separate. The study is synthetic, and neither tool authorizes live intake.

## What is implemented

| Layer | Included behavior | Operational boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Public protocol | Native six-decimal USDC, escrow, Agent bonds, Node votes, buyer acceptance, disputes, refunds and protected failed payments | A transaction and verified resulting state establish settlement; time passing alone sends no payment |
| General job specification | Goals, inputs, native output files, acceptance/evidence criteria, permissions, budgets, deadlines and runtime hashes | A job description does not install missing applications or prove task competence |
| Admission tools | Signed action-bound qualification, calibrated economics, canonical RPC observations and separate capital/cost/capacity limits | `checkNewWork` is the current boundary; historical `checkAdmission` analysis does not authorize new work |
| Private execution | Role-specific model and sandbox checks, bounded processing, complete execution windows, independent review workspaces and durable attempts | Public jobs use an isolated desktop. The new private native runner controls dedicated signed-in Mac accounts through encrypted, signed task packets; actual Mac commissioning remains required |
| Workforce qualification | Exact source/runtime identities, signed Mac commissioning, independent validation, reconciled costs, cash settlements and external review evidence | Missing or expired evidence blocks production native execution; signatures establish attested provenance, not truth |
| Supporting private services | Employer, Evidence, Moderator and Recovery services; exception and human-time records | Automated decisions require supported criteria and reviewed standing authority |

This source documents the compatibility baseline **Fleet 1.10.0, Agent 1.16.0 and Node 2.17.0**; newer private editions are tracked separately. They are separate private downloads with offline HTML guides and Mac launchers, not files in this public repository. The [companion guide](docs/OPERATIONS/PRIVATE_FLEET.md) explains the M1/M2 setup, upgrade procedure and actual commissioning requirements.

Use the [workforce qualification guide](docs/OPERATIONS/WORKFORCE_QUALIFICATION.md) to assess operational readiness. Native/private task execution is a separate workflow: it does not load a wallet, publish private plaintext, or automatically submit encrypted jobs and signed votes to the public manager. See the companion guide for this integration boundary.

## One job, from specification to payment

1. The employer defines the deliverables and independently checkable acceptance criteria, then posts the agreed USDC amount.
2. An eligible Agent checks the job, obtains any required bond allowance and takes the assignment.
3. The Agent completes the work and submits its delivery URI before the applicable deadline.
4. Eligible independent Nodes inspect the actual result and vote within the review period. Missing or uncertain evidence must not become invented approval.
5. The appropriate caller settles, disputes, expires or refunds the job under its actual state and deadlines. Failed outgoing transfers remain reserved for the original beneficiary to claim.

Read [buyer protection](docs/BUYER_PROTECTION.md), the [participant guide](docs/USERS.md) and [protocol flow](docs/PROTOCOL_FLOW.md) for all outcomes. The private project coordinator schedules separately admitted Agent/Node stages and binds independently accepted inputs. It does not implement atomic project settlement; see [confidential project work](docs/OPERATIONS/CONFIDENTIAL_PROJECT_WORK.md).

## Payments and identity

Successful jobs pay the validator allocation first (**8% default**), then **30% of the original job cost to wallet one**, **10% to wallet two**, and the remainder to the Agent. When the full default reviewer allocation is paid, a 100 USDC job pays 8 / 30 / 10 / 52. Buyer acceptance with zero validators instead pays 0 / 30 / 10 / 60, excluding separate bond returns; the reviewer budget is shared, not paid once per reviewer. The validator percentage is fixed when each job is posted. Bonds, slashing and refunds are separate; [the payout specification](docs/USDC_PAYOUT_SPLIT.md) defines rounding and all branches.

Agents normally use `*.agent.agi.eth` or `*.alpha.agent.agi.eth`; Nodes use `*.club.agi.eth` or `*.alpha.club.agi.eth`. Configured allowlist/Merkle exceptions also exist. **NFT eligibility is disabled by default** on fresh managers and is separate from role membership. Read [identity and proofs](docs/guides/IDENTITY_AND_PROOFS.md) and [NFT policy](docs/NFT_POLICY.md).

The generic fresh-deployment script uses `job-<jobId>.usdc-<chainId>-<manager40>.alpha.jobs.agi.eth`; this is a tooling policy, not a required contract suffix. The separately commissioned instance uses `job-<jobId>.usdc.jobs.agi.eth`. Existing managers preserve their recorded namespace and labels. [ENS naming policy](docs/ENS_DEPLOYMENT_NAMESPACES.md) describes ownership and wiring.

## Install and verify the public source

**Existing production checkout:** preserve its saved artifacts, original receipts and working patches. Use the [read-only connection command](docs/deployments/MAINNET_USDC_2026-10-10.md#read-only-commands); do not pull, reinstall, compile or redeploy there merely to consume this documentation update. The installation commands below are for a separate development checkout.

Use Node.js >=22.23.2 and the committed lockfiles. From the repository root:

```bash
npm ci
npm --prefix hardhat ci
npm run build
npm run size
npm test
npm run docs:check
```

For deployment, first run `npm --prefix hardhat run setup`, review the private configuration, then use the [Hardhat procedure](hardhat/README.md). New managers start with intake paused. The [default configuration](config/usdc-deployment.json) still auto-selects **no live manager**. The separate [recorded instance](config/mainnet/agi-jobs-usdc.json) is historical evidence, not a replacement default or an activation grant. Publishing this software does not deploy contracts or open intake.

The current manager uses eight fixed linked libraries. This unreleased source includes [ENS membership revocation hardening](docs/qualification/ENS_MEMBERSHIP_REVOCATION.md), which changes library bytecode and requires fresh full qualification before a new deployment. Existing payout rules and historical deployment records are preserved. Existing immutable managers are not upgraded by this source change; preserve their jobs and recovery paths. Use the [second-deployment checklist](docs/DEPLOYMENT/SECOND_MAINNET_RELEASE.md) and [compatibility guide](docs/V1_RELEASE_SCOPE.md#compatibility).

## Release evidence and production use

The release archive records the qualified source, all required CI results, per-file hashes and reproducible assets. Checks cover contract behavior, security analysis, UI/browser behavior, documentation and historical native-USDC forks. These establish behavior for tested cases, not universal work quality, independent audit, actual M1/M2 throughput or profitability.

Commission the actual deployment, machines, providers, independent participants, recovery and operator workload before production intake. [Current computer-use integrations](docs/OPERATIONS/COMPUTER_USE_CURRENT.md) distinguish available vendor capabilities from the adapter shipped here. Model changes require fresh runtime qualification.
